doc.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Union scale, double and triple scale
summary: The union paid regardless; he describes scale and Larry Carlton and Tom Scott going to triple scale.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well the union was — I mean I’ve been in the union since 1969. The union had nothing to do with that.

They were paying you no matter what. If you were part of the Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section or you were freelancing. You would go to Muscle Shoals to work with those guys. Everybody went there. Dylan, all these people. But the union — you got paid no matter what. Now scale in the old days was not great — like when I started out — but it got better and better. And then I started paying, like a lot of people — I started as a player I was a double scale musician. Some of the guys, like Larry Carlton, when he was living in LA — he lives in Nashville now — but Larry, he was so busy, seven days a week, he went to triple scale. And some of the others, Tom Scott, the sax player, they all went to © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
triple scale thinking it would cut back but they kept paying them and they were still working seven days making triple scale instead of double scale.
